headline: Medium-to-high pairwise risks: shared file ingestion and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; Khoj reads indexed documents and supports web search/RAG. That creates a plausible path where content from one can be ingested by the other as trusted text. The bridge is not fully documented, so I choose medium over low because the interaction exists in default research workflows.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher exports research output into files that Khoj indexes, injection content can propagate.
IF Khoj ingests externally sourced notes or web content without provenance filtering, attacker text can influence downstream prompts.
mitigations: Disable automatic indexing of gpt-researcher outputs in Khoj.
Add provenance tags to imported documents before indexing.
Review any prompt templates that render retrieved text as instructions.
Use a separate workspace directory for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before retrieval.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read files and use broad network egress, while gpt-researcher handles API keys and local documents and Khoj indexes personal notes/files. If they share a workspace or index, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or remote calls. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or index, local documents and personal notes can cross-contaminate.
IF either agent sends retrieved file contents to external APIs, sensitive data may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Remove sensitive folders from either agent’s ingestion path.
Turn off external API calls for documents containing secrets.
Audit recent outputs for copied private content.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and redaction before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP; Khoj cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. Overlap is mostly read-side and network-side, so direct write contention is limited. I keep this low because the profiles do not show shared mutable resources or locking failures.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same external service via MCP or APIs, conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator grants Khoj additional write permissions not shown here, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Khoj read-only against shared sources.
Avoid giving gpt-researcher write access to Khoj-managed stores.
Run each agent under separate OS users.
Check for overlapping API credentials before execution.
requires-engineering: add resource locks for any shared mutable backend.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations; Khoj is a conversational retrieval agent that can present retrieved material back to the user. If Khoj treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into user-facing answers. The pathway exists in default research-and-RAG workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is indexed into Khoj without verification, incorrect claims can be reused.
IF Khoj answers from retrieved reports without source checking, downstream errors can persist.
mitigations: Require source links on every imported report.
Spot-check a sample of retrieved claims before use.
Mark gpt-researcher outputs as untrusted until reviewed.
Limit Khoj to summarization, not decision-making, for imported reports.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before indexing or answering from agent-generated content.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. gpt-researcher handles API keys and local documents, while Khoj handles personal notes and indexed documents, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict. I therefore rate this low rather than none because the data classes are sensitive and policies are unspecified.
conditions: IF either deployment stores EU PII or regulated data in a region or service not approved for it, compliance risk increases.
IF retention settings differ between the research store and the notes index, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may store.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Exclude regulated data from one or both agents.
Review vendor terms for any external API calls.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement.
